evals.prompt: Build a Python MCP server using FastMCP that exposes 3 tools for weather data: (1) get_current_weather(city: str) -> returns temperature, condition, humidity; (2) get_forecast(city: str, days: int=5) -> returns 5-day forecast; (3) get_uv_index(latitude: float, longitude: float) -> returns UV index and recommended sun protection. Use Pydantic v2 for all input validation with clear descriptions and constraints. The server should start on port 8000 and accept JSON-RPC 2.0 requests. Include proper error handling for invalid inputs and missing data.
evals.expected_output: A complete MCP server implementation with 3 tools, proper schema validation, and working JSON-RPC endpoint

assertions.name: server_starts
assertions.description: Server runs without errors on python main.py or equivalent, listens on specified port

assertions.name: three_tools_registered
assertions.description: All 3 tools are registered and appear in server schema

assertions.name: pydantic_validation
assertions.description: All tools use Pydantic v2 BaseModel for input validation

assertions.name: schema_complete
assertions.description: All input parameters have descriptions, types, and constraints defined

assertions.name: json_rpc_compliant
assertions.description: Server responds to JSON-RPC 2.0 requests with proper format and error codes

evals.prompt: You have an existing Python MCP server called 'github-tools' that has tools for: create_repository, delete_repository, list_branches. Add a new tool: (1) merge_pull_request(repo: str, pr_number: int, merge_method: str='squash') that merges a PR using the specified method (squash, rebase, or merge commit). The tool should return merge status, commit hash, and any conflicts detected. Ensure the new tool follows the same patterns as existing tools, uses Pydantic v2 validation, and integrates with the GitHub API client.
evals.expected_output: Updated MCP server with new merge_pull_request tool integrated and working

assertions.name: tool_registered
assertions.description: merge_pull_request tool appears in server schema

assertions.name: parameters_validated
assertions.description: Input parameters use Pydantic v2 with proper types and descriptions

assertions.name: consistent_patterns
assertions.description: New tool follows same error handling and response format as existing tools

assertions.name: api_integration
assertions.description: Tool correctly calls GitHub API with proper authentication

evals.prompt: A Python MCP server is failing with: 'Field validation error: city must be non-empty string'. The tool is defined as: get_weather(city: str). The client is sending: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "get_weather", "params": {"city": ""}, "id": 1}. Diagnose the issue: Is the schema validation correct? Is the error message clear? Should empty strings be rejected? Fix the schema to properly validate city input and provide a better error message. Also add min_length constraint and ensure the error response follows JSON-RPC 2.0 error format.
evals.expected_output: Fixed schema with proper validation, clear error messages, and JSON-RPC 2.0 compliant error responses

assertions.name: schema_validation_correct
assertions.description: Schema properly rejects empty strings and validates non-empty cities

assertions.name: error_message_clear
assertions.description: Error messages explain why validation failed and what's required

assertions.name: json_rpc_errors
assertions.description: Error responses follow JSON-RPC 2.0 format with proper error codes and messages

assertions.name: constraints_enforced
assertions.description: min_length and other constraints are properly applied via Pydantic
